root_cause.text: The function `target_tg_pt_gp_members_show()` uses the return value of `snprintf()` as the length for `memcpy()` without verifying that it does not exceed the stack buffer size (`TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF`), allowing an out-of-bounds read when `snprintf()` truncates the output due to long fabric WWNs (e.g., iSCSI IQN names up to 223 bytes).
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (cur_len > TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF)` before the `memcpy()`, and the commit message states: "snprintf() returns the length the output would have had, which can exceed the buffer size ... The check at the memcpy() site only guards the destination page write, not the source read, so memcpy() will read past the stack buffer and copy adjacent stack contents."

This bounds check only ensures the total output fits within the page buffer (PAGE_SIZE), but does not verify that the snprintf() return value (len) is within the stack buffer size TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF. This allows an out-of-bounds read when len is larger than the stack buffer.
